text:
maria_cs: Hey team — customer (AcmePayments) reporting intermittent 429s and large tail latency spikes when they hit burst traffic (spikes up to ~150 rps). They say it looks like "throttling" because some requests return quickly while others timeout. Headers attached from their client: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 100`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `X-RateLimit-Reset: 24s`.
julian_runtime: thanks @maria_cs, can you paste sample request pattern and whether they use streaming? also which model/route? :eyes:
maria_cs: streaming=false, route=/v1/generate, model=redwood-13b-qat, bursts are short (20-40s) but very high concurrency. They use our hosted API with default quota. Repro steps they gave:
```
for i in $(seq 1 200); do curl -s -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"payment confirmation","max_tokens":64}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
tara_oncall: I've seen this pattern before. Two likely interacting factors: continuous batching latency + KV cache cold misses. When a tenant bursts, many requests land with empty KV cache, the runtime needs to build KV state which raises p50/p95 for those requests. Continuous batching then groups some of the warm requests but the cold ones get delayed, and our per-tenant concurrency guard kicks in -> 429s for extra inflight requests. 
kai_sre: pinging infra-bot to pull logs for tenant acme-prod during the window. infra-bot: fetching logs from 2024-10-12T15:03:00Z..2024-10-12T15:05:00Z for tenant acme-prod: 4,372 requests, 7.8% 429, median latency 48ms, p95 870ms, p99 2.3s. Matched spike in KV-cache miss rate ~61%.
julian_runtime: that KV cache miss rate is huge. Do we have their tenant config? specifically `max_batch_size`, `max_batch_delay_ms`, and `kv_cache.enabled`?
maria_cs: customer config: `max_batch_size: 64`, `max_batch_delay_ms: 25`, `kv_cache: enabled (default)`, no dedicated capacity.
alex_engineering: here's an explanation: continuous batching aims to collect requests for up to `max_batch_delay_ms`. If you have many concurrent cold requests that all require building KV cache, the initial token generation for each will hold the GPU longer. That increases observed latency and reduces effective throughput. Our tenant-level concurrency limiter (default 100) will start returning 429s for additional requests beyond the soft limit.
maria_cs: Customer wants to know: is this "throttling" or a bug? They also saw `x-retry-after: 1` on a few 429s.
julian_runtime: it's not a bug per-se; it's a coupling of features. Two mitigation paths:
1) client-side: shape the burst, add jitter and exponential backoff; lower concurrency and pre-warm cache by sending a few warmup requests before a large burst. Example script:
```
# quick prewarm
for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"warm","max_tokens":8}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; done
```
2) server-side: we can temporarily increase tenant concurrency, reduce `max_batch_delay_ms` to 5-10ms for them, and enable aggressive KV prefetching for common prefixes. Also consider Reserved/Dedicated capacity if bursts are steady.
kai_sre: added temporary quota bump for acme-prod: concurrency soft limit -> 250, burst window increased; note this will increase cost. I also opened infra ticket INF-8763 to check autoscale headroom during those windows.
maria_cs: customer asked for reproability — they want a script to reproduce exactly what they saw so support can show root cause. julian_runtime: ok here's a repro that mirrors their pattern but marks the headers and collects timing:
```
# repro.py
import requests, time, threading
TOKEN = "REDACTED"
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate"
def hit():
  t0 = time.time()
  r = requests.post(url, headers={"Authorization":f"Bearer {TOKEN}"}, json={"input":"payment","max_tokens":64})
  print(r.status_code, r.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Remaining'), round((time.time()-t0)*1000))
threads = []
for i in range(200):
  t = threading.Thread(target=hit)
  t.start(); threads.append(t)
  if i%20==0: time.sleep(0.02)
for t in threads: t.join()
```
julian_runtime: running that locally against staging reproduced 6% 429s and p95 ~ 900ms. The staging runtime showed KV cold loads spiking in trace.
alex_engineering: short-term fix applied: reduced `max_batch_delay_ms` to 8ms for acme-prod, enabled "prefix_kv_prefetch" flag for their tenant, and warmed top-10 most common prompts via scheduled warm calls. We also surfaced `X-Tenant-Concurrency` and `X-Tenant-Burst` headers for observability.
maria_cs: I informed the customer and they ran tests. They report much fewer 429s and median latency improved. :tada:
tara_oncall: follow-ups: - document this pattern in our KB (support playbook) - product to expose burst tuning UI - sales to discuss Dedicated for customers with predictable high bursts
kai_sre: filing postmortem note: root cause = high cold KV miss rate interacting with continuous batching and tenant concurrency limits; remediation = tenant-specific batching tuning + temporary concurrency bump + pre-warm + education.
alex_engineering: leaving a small config snippet used:
```
tenant_config:
  max_batch_delay_ms: 8
  max_batch_size: 64
  tenant_concurrency_soft_limit: 250
  kv_cache_prefetch_prefixes: ["confirm", "payment", "invoice"]
```
maria_cs: closing loop with the customer, they've asked for a long-term recommendation: Dedicated or set up scheduled pre-warms before business-critical bursts. I've scheduled a call with Sales + Solutions next week.
julian_runtime: adding note: we'll upstream an internal telemetry change to expose per-tenant KV miss rate in Console so these patterns are easier to diagnose.
maria_cs: thanks everyone — marking resolved for now, will reopen if they see regression. :white_check_mark:
